title: Compact SO(5) dynamics stably aligns the two vector copies, but continuation does not preserve the potential symmetry

claim.statement: A simple SO(5)-invariant Gram potential stably selects a rank-one two-vector vacuum with SO(4) stabilizer, and the selected algebraic configuration can be continued to a timelike Spin(2,3) compensator with SO(1,3) stabilizer.
claim.cost: The Euclidean positivity responsible for stability is not Spin(2,3)-invariant; the Cartan involution or real-form selection must therefore enter as physical structure.

continuation.lost: Cauchy-Schwarz positivity of the Euclidean Gram determinant
continuation.warning: Replacing the Euclidean metric in the potential by the invariant (2,3) metric reproduces the v656 negative modes and null runaway.

interpretation: Vacuum selection in the compact parent followed by real-form continuation is much better behaved than trying to minimize a noncompact invariant potential directly.
This gives the programme a concrete staged research route: compact spectral dynamics first, geometric real-form interpretation second.
The route is not neutral: it introduces a preferred Cartan involution/positive inner product whose origin and observability must be explained.
falsifiers: A fully Spin(2,3)-invariant bounded potential that stably yields the same aligned vacuum would remove the need for compact-first selection.
If the continued kinetic/action signs are inconsistent, algebraic continuation of the vacuum is insufficient.
Quantum corrections could destabilize the compact alignment and remain untested.
nextBranches: Use the existing carrier Cartan involution to write the positive alignment norm intrinsically and identify its residual symmetry.
Audit whether the continued MacDowell-Mansouri action has the correct Einstein-Hilbert sign for each choice of timelike compensator.
Formulate the compact-to-real continuation as a phase-selection rule with explicit order parameters.
